featured.line: of hydropower potential at one site, on one river
featured.name: Inga Falls
featured.text: The Congo carries the second-largest flow of any river on Earth. Inga 1 and Inga 2 use about 1.8 GW of it; the rest still runs to the sea.
featured.alt: White water and mist on the lower Congo River at Inga

featured.line: the size of the island: the sea Barbados governs
featured.name: The Barbados Sea
featured.text: An exclusive economic zone of more than 185,000 km² around an island of about 430 km². Fisheries, tourism, blue carbon and blue bonds draw on the same water.
featured.source: CRFM, Barbados Marine Spatial Planning Profile
featured.alt: Turquoise shallows falling into deep blue water off Barbados

featured.line: of Botswana’s exports were diamonds in 2023
featured.name: The Diamonds
featured.text: Mined by Debswana, owned in equal shares by the Government of Botswana and De Beers. The 2025 agreement raises the state’s share of Debswana’s sales to 30%, then 40%.
featured.alt: The terraced open pit of a diamond mine in the Kalahari at sunset

featured.line: of railway from the Atlantic to the Congo border
featured.name: The Lobito Corridor
featured.text: The Benguela line runs from the port of Lobito to Luau, the shortest route from the mineral belts of the Congo and Zambia to the sea. A route earns every time something moves along it.
featured.alt: The Lobito Atlantic Railway in Angola

featured.name: The Sun
featured.text: Now the largest part of 299 GW of renewable capacity.
featured.source: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy, physical progress, 30 September 2026
